prompt:
Draft a procedure for handling customer complaints at an electronics contract manufacturer. Include intake channels, severity classification, initial response timelines, investigation methodology, 8D report format, customer communication cadence, systemic trending, and closure criteria. Align with ISO 9001 clauses 8.2.1 and 10.2.

Return a single JSON object with EXACTLY these fields:
- document (string): the complete procedure or document text
- sections (string): structured sections of the document
- clauseRefs (string): ISO clause references addressed

End your response with exactly one line: ANSWER: <your JSON object>
response:
{
  "document": "1. PURPOSE
This procedure establishes a standardized process for receiving, classifying, investigating, resolving, and closing customer complaints at [Company Name], an electronics contract manufacturer. It ensures compliance with ISO 9001:2015 clauses 8.2.1 (Customer Communication) and 10.2 (Nonconformity and Corrective Action) by promoting timely response, root cause analysis, and systemic improvement.

2. SCOPE
Applies to all customer complaints received regarding product quality, delivery, documentation, or service related to manufactured electronic assemblies and components.

3. DEFINITIONS
- Customer Complaint: Any formal or informal expression of dissatisfaction by a customer regarding a product or service provided by [Company Name].
- Severity Classification: Categorization of complaints based on impact (Critical, Major, Minor).
- 8D Report: Eight Disciplines problem-solving methodology used for root cause analysis and corrective action.
- Systemic Trending: Analysis of complaint data over time to identify recurring issues.

4. INTAKE CHANNELS
Customer complaints may be received via:
- Email: complaints@company.com (primary)
- Customer Portal: Secure online form on company website
- Phone: Dedicated hotline (800-XXX-XXXX)
- Fax: 800-XXX-XXXX
- In-Person: During site visits or audits
All complaints must be logged within 1 hour of receipt into the Quality Management System (QMS) database with unique complaint ID, date/time, customer name, product ID, and description.

5. SEVERITY CLASSIFICATION
Complaints are classified within 2 hours of intake:
- Critical (C1): Safety hazard, regulatory noncompliance, complete product failure affecting production line, or customer shutdown.
- Major (C2): Functional failure, significant performance deviation, or impact on customer’s end product.
- Minor (C3): Cosmetic defect, documentation error, or minor delay not impacting functionality.

6. INITIAL RESPONSE TIMELINES
- Critical (C1): Acknowledge within 1 hour; initial response (containment plan) within 4 hours.
- Major (C2): Acknowledge within 4 hours; initial response within 24 hours.
- Minor (C3): Acknowledge within 24 hours; initial response within 5 business days.
Response must include complaint ID, assigned owner, estimated resolution timeline, and contact information.

7. INVESTIGATION METHODOLOGY
All complaints classified as C1 or C2 require a formal investigation using the 8D methodology. C3 complaints may use a simplified 3-step process (Root Cause, Action, Verification). Investigation includes:
- Review of production records, test data, inspection reports, and shipping logs.
- Physical inspection of returned product (if available).
- Interviews with production, QA, and logistics personnel.
- Use of tools: 5 Whys, Fishbone Diagram, FMEA.
Investigation must be completed within:
- C1: 5 business days
- C2: 10 business days
- C3: 15 business days

8. 8D REPORT FORMAT
The 8D report must include:
D1: Team Formation — List members, roles, and contact info.
D2: Problem Description — Clear, concise, quantified statement with data.
D3: Interim Containment Actions — Actions taken to protect customer.
D4: Root Cause Analysis — Validated using 5 Whys or Fishbone.
D5: Permanent Corrective Actions (PCA) — Specific, measurable, assignable.
D6: Implementation of PCA — Dates, responsible parties, evidence.
D7: Preventive Actions — Systemic changes to prevent recurrence (e.g., SOP updates, training, process controls).
D8: Team Recognition & Closure — Sign-off by QA Manager and Customer Liaison.
All 8D reports are stored in QMS with audit trail.

9. CUSTOMER COMMUNICATION CADENCE
- C1: Daily updates until resolution; final report within 7 days.
- C2: Bi-weekly updates; final report within 14 days.
- C3: One update at resolution; final report within 21 days.
All communications must be documented in QMS and include: date, sender, recipient, summary, and action items.

10. SYSTEMIC TRENDING
Monthly, the Quality Department generates a complaint trend report using QMS data, analyzing:
- Frequency by product line, process step, or customer.
- Recurrence of root causes.
- Effectiveness of PCAs.
Trends triggering action: ≥3 occurrences of same root cause in 90 days → initiate Process Improvement Project (PIP).
Trend reports are reviewed by Management Review (ISO 9001:2015 clause 9.3).

11. CLOSURE CRITERIA
A complaint is closed only when:
- Customer acknowledges resolution in writing (email or portal confirmation).
- All corrective and preventive actions are implemented and verified.
- 8D report is fully completed and approved.
- Systemic changes are documented and communicated.
- No further complaints of same nature occur within 60 days of closure.
Closure is recorded in QMS with final sign-off by QA Manager.

12. RECORDS
All complaint records, 8D reports, and trend analyses are retained for minimum 7 years per ISO 9001 requirements.

13. RESPONSIBILITIES
- Customer Service: Intake and initial response.
- Quality Assurance: Investigation, 8D management, trending.
- Production/Engineering: Implement PCAs.
- Management: Review trends, approve PCAs, ensure resource allocation.

14. REFERENCES
- ISO 9001:2015 Clauses 8.2.1, 10.2
- Company QMS Manual, Section 8.5.2
- 8D Problem Solving Standard (Internal Document Q-8D-001)",
